intro.text: A world-sized structure made of countless rooms, stacked on and around each other and always on the move.
A planet-wide megastructure whose cities are built from thousands of shared, moving rooms, all run by one vast central Invested mechanism.

description.text: A resident who wants a room for a particular purpose, such as sleeping or bathing, asks the Apparatus, and a suitable room is brought to join the one they are in. Sunlight is rare, reached only by asking for a room with windows, which then travels to the edge. People keep their belongings in trunks that move with them, and because every room is shared, no one owns any space.

Its people hold that their spirits only borrow their bodies, much as they borrow rooms. They tell of "the gravelands", where the Apparatus dumps rooms that have broken down or worn out, along with anyone unlucky enough to be inside.
Many peoples live there, Lawnarks among them, held in bondage by a ruling class of Sleepless who experiment on the mortal residents. No birds live on the Apparatus.

Life under watchful Sleepless has shaped the residents' culture: they tend to be wordy and proud of the technology they won over centuries of struggle for freedom. Few crews take jobs near the Apparatus, so the work there pays well. Outsiders often expect its people to be simple folk dazzled by the wider world, when in fact they are more advanced than most planets.
